title: card-060 — Verus compile errors say a struct field is not a method when a stored spec function is applied directly to an argument in a proof
content: **Trigger:** Verus compile errors say a struct field is not a method when a stored spec function is applied directly to an argument in a proof. **Action:** Rewrite each occurrence so the field projection is parenthesized first and then applied to the index argument. After fixing parsing, if Verus reports a missing trigger for the universal equality, add explicit trigger annotations to both sides of the equality. **Why:** The field stores a function value rather than a method, so the parser needs the projection to be treated as a callable value. The explicit trigger then lets the pointwise equality quantifier instantiate at arbitrary indices so the execution equality lemma can be applied. **Validate:** Re-run Verus; compile errors should vanish. If a subsequent trigger error appears, adding the explicit trigger should enable verification, and the final proof should pass with all proof functions verified and the safety comparison clean. **Avoid when:** The field is not a function-valued field, or the equality can be proved by another supplied lemma without pointwise expansion; fixing syntax does not replace a missing logical fact.
